html:
A state of Dyula Muslim traders centred on the town of Kong in the north of today's Ivory Coast, built up in the early 18th century by Sekou Ouattara.

Kong sat between the forest, which produced kola nuts and gold, and the markets of the Niger bend, and its merchants carried cloth, salt and kola across the region. It was also a centre of Islamic learning. Its power faded in the 19th century, and in 1897 the army of Samori Ture, retreating east from the French, burned the town. France then took the north into its colony. See also the Mande peoples and the trans-Saharan trade.
